gen-megrim-fs-karma: Karma is a trustworthy serif, its terminals stopping short of the stem. Megrim is at its best as angular, futuristic display lettering, while Karma is at its best as classic running text.
gen-gf-tektur-montserrat: Pipe-cleaner curves with outsized lowercase proportions give Tektur its expressive, distinctive look at the top of the pair. Montserrat, geometric and approachable, does best with a slightly generous body size.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-switzer: Text here reads in thin, wire-like strokes whose c tips never creep toward touching. Switzer, approachable and Swiss in temperament, handles the reading, while Tilt Neon takes the loud, tube-like commanding lines.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-asap: Asap keeps its c forms as open arcs and its body height close to the capitals, steady and readable. Heavy, widely tracked Dogica against that readable body gives pure contrast.
gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-supreme: Gaps where paper shows through: that's Wallpoet, bold and commanding. Supreme lays a thick, crisp strip of text beneath it, so the see-through heading and solid body hold each other in place.
gen-luckiest-guy-manrope: A high-set mean line and poured-ink strokes make Luckiest Guy cheerful and loud. But Manrope keeps a bright open gap at every curve, so the text stays approachable and clean.
gen-press-start-2p-switzer: Press Start 2P spaces its letters like cut-outs pinned far apart. It earns its keep when big and short, while Switzer, approachable and Swiss, keeps tubular strokes that never vary in weight.
gen-dafont-impact-label-fs-asap: Commanding and heavy, Impact Label sets each letter alone like a bead on a rod, with its c ends splayed like pincers. Asap keeps its open arcs readable beneath it.
gen-dafont-galaxy-fs-merriweather-sans: Words here look large and weighty, a good counterweight to cosmic, commanding Galaxy. Merriweather Sans lets its e open clearly to the right, so a longer run of text stays clear and sturdy.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-asap: Powerful and ancient, Nordic sets wirelike strokes of one thickness with cramped, closed letters spaced like brush dabs. Asap's open arcs give those closed heading letters a readable, open-handed counterpart.
